chain.statement: Other BUBR1 truncations show transcript loss consistent with nonsense-mediated decay, so the nonsense allele is expected to yield little stable protein.
Other MVA-associated BUBR1 missense mutants show reduced abundance and increased turnover, so residual-protein stability may govern the missense allele.
Forcing two other mutants to wild-type levels restored the nocodazole checkpoint response in a replacement-cell assay, so abundance can limit function for those alleles.
Too little functional BUBR1 weakens the spindle checkpoint and allows chromosome mis-segregation in dividing cells.
Whether the two alleles lie in trans is unresolved without phasing data.
Mosaic aneuploidy contributes to the growth failure and rhabdomyosarcoma in this child.

harm_directions: Further weakening the spindle checkpoint, for example with checkpoint-kinase inhibitors or microtubule poisons offered as rescue
Lowering residual BUBR1, since HSP90 inhibition reduced mutant BUBR1 abundance in cells
Agents that conflict with the anticipated rhabdomyosarcoma regimen
unknowns: Phase of the two alleles (trans or cis)
Transcript and protein level contributed by each allele in the patient's own cells
Whether the missense allele is unstable or catalytically inactive, noting BUBR1 is a pseudokinase
